clue.text: Eradicated what could make set damp?

indicators.note: the answer's second word is itself an instruction to rearrange, and the clue asks what such an instruction could turn into those letters

blocks.note: these seven letters rearranged form the first word
the familiar anagram signal word, here supplied as part of the solution

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what might have dampened a set of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: STAMPED OUT, read as an instruction, means 'rearrange STAMPED', and that rearrangement can give SET DAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp out a disease or practice is to destroy it completely, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Views appropriate broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so we go by the sound of the word

blocks.note: to appropriate is to seize or take over

explanation.surface: Opinions that are suitable to be aired on air.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, views and sees both mean looks at or regards something.

clue.text: Lured cat with treat prepared by daughter

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked over and made into something new, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A pet coaxed in with a snack that a girl has put together.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure is to tempt or draw in, the same as to have attracted someone.

clue.text: Criticise current Conservative anxiety

blocks.note: critics pan a show they dislike
I is the physics symbol for electric current
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a topical Tory worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, an intense form of anxiety.

clue.text: Blames diet, oddly, then weeps

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep only the letters in the first, third and other odd positions

blocks.note: first and third letters of the word
to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: A dieter faults their regime in a strange way and bursts into tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To decry something is to denounce it publicly, close in sense to blaming or condemning it.

clue.text: Joanna, perhaps, is respectable

blocks.note: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for a piano
an ... citizen is honest and respectable

explanation.walkthrough: Joanna looks like a woman's name; in Cockney rhyming slang it means piano (Joanna rhymes with 'pianner'), and 'perhaps' marks UPRIGHT as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a piano with vertical strings, and an upright person is morally honourable.

clue.text: The setter entertained by Queen with very loud guitar music?

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken inside, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
the setter refers to themself as I
fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: The compiler hosted by the rock band Queen, playing deafening guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen the rock band fits the guitar surface but is just R here.
explanation.definitionFit: A riff is a short repeated phrase of music, typically played on guitar in rock; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Not entirely drastic EU price freeze

indicators.note: not entirely means we use only part of the following words, a run of letters straddling them

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of the first word and ends in the third

explanation.surface: A partial freeze on prices imposed by Brussels that stops short of drastic.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice up is to become covered or blocked with ice, which is to freeze.

clue.text: Felt these bats will circle adult – these often come out at night

definitions.text: these often come out at night

indicators.note: bats as an adjective means crazy, so these letters go haywire into a new order
to circle something is to go round it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: nine letters to be rearranged
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Bats circling over someone's head, nocturnal creatures being the theme.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats and coming out at night suggest the animals, but bats is the anagram signal and the night-time habit belongs to dentures taken out before bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are commonly removed at bedtime, so they come out at night.

clue.text: Drinks when drunk could make Bruno sob

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, and so are these letters

blocks.note: eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Too many whiskies leave a man named Bruno in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the other way round: the answer, when its letters are mixed up, could spell BRUNO SOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourbons are American whiskeys, so they are an example of drinks.

clue.text: Scoffed each time gent stripped

indicators.note: something stripped has its outer layer taken off, so the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
T is the abbreviation for time
the word without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A man undressing to the jeers of onlookers every time.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is British slang for gobbling it, so scoffed food has been eaten.

clue.text: Physical energy conserved by officer

indicators.note: something conserved by a keeper is held safely inside it

blocks.note: a corporal is a non-commissioned officer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A soldier with the bodily stamina to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means having a body, so it is a synonym of physical as opposed to spiritual.

clue.text: The same competition in golf

blocks.note: a match is a sporting contest
taken as written
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Describing two identical tournaments on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching items are identical or alike, so they are the same.

clue.text: Regret entertaining heads of private enterprises for money

indicators.note: heads are the tops of things, so we keep only the opening letter of each word
a host entertaining guests has them inside, so letters go within

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Remorse over hosting business bosses just to raise cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India and Pakistan, an example of money.

clue.text: Leave for a diplomatic errand

blocks.note: per means for each or for a, as in miles per hour
a mission is an official errand abroad

explanation.surface: An envoy taking time off to go on official business.
explanation.walkthrough: Leave looks like a verb, but here it is the noun meaning consent.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave in the sense of 'by your leave' is formal permission to do something.

clue.text: Meal servings in French planes?

blocks.note: en is the French for in
the plane is a tree, common in London streets

explanation.surface: Dinners served on French aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Planes conjures aircraft and in-flight meals; here it means the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrées are courses of a meal, either a main dish or one served before it.

clue.text: Still working after small garage's first service

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word before it
after places the word before it later in the answer than the word that follows

blocks.note: still and even both intensify a comparison: even better, still better
S is the abbreviation for small
a machine that is on is working
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A car still running after its first service at a little garage.
explanation.walkthrough: The car-service surface hides a church service; 'working after small' puts ON after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, so it is an example of a service.

clue.text: Problems from initially toasting Russian bread

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so we take only the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
bread is slang for money, and the rouble is Russia's currency

explanation.surface: Kitchen mishaps from grilling slices of Russian loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, not the loaf the toasting suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble as a mass noun means difficulties or worries, the same as problems.

clue.text: One insect underneath fish is out of sight

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing underneath another comes later in the answer

blocks.note: the brill is a European flatfish
the Roman numeral for one
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug hiding beneath a fish so it cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'underneath' puts the one-and-insect after the fish. Out of sight looks literal, but it is dated slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Out of sight' was 1960s slang praise meaning wonderful, matching brilliant in its colloquial sense.

clue.text: Crowd swallowing conclusion about insanity

indicators.note: whatever is swallowed ends up inside the swallower
about can mean turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a mass is a large crowd of people
the end is the conclusion

explanation.surface: A mob that believes a madcap theory about the end of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness is a straightforward synonym for insanity, mental illness or extreme folly.

clue.text: Swimmer unhappy crossing river in Spain

indicators.note: to cross something here is to span it, so the word lies around the letter

blocks.note: unhappy means sad
R is the abbreviation for river
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A melancholy swimmer making it across a Spanish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords often call a fish a swimmer, and the sardine is a small fish.

clue.text: Black animal is perfect, ultimately, for musician

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so we keep only the final letter

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an ass is a donkey
taken as written
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dark-coated beast turns out to be just right for a band member.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassist plays the bass guitar or double bass, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Rest book on a weapon

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written
a lance is a knight's spear

explanation.surface: Instruction to prop a volume against a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: Rest looks like a verb paired with book; it is the noun meaning what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The balance of a sum is the remainder, the same as the rest of it.

clue.text: The woman's clothing Penny removes

indicators.note: clothing is a verb here: to clothe something is to wrap it up inside

blocks.note: she's is the contraction of she is or she has
D was the symbol for the old British penny, from Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny taking off her clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothing looks like a noun Penny takes off; it is the verb wrapping SHE'S round D.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something, such as skin or a coat, is to cast it off or remove it.

clue.text: Wax lyrical about former lover to student

blocks.note: an ex is a past partner
taken as written
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone gushing about an old flame to a student.
explanation.walkthrough: About belongs to the definition, not a reversal or container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically, which is what waxing lyrical about something means.

clue.text: All beer I brewed is good

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together into something new, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A home-brewer declaring every beer they make a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Good can mean dependable, as in good for a loan, which is what reliable means.

clue.text: More bananas, unopened, for snake

indicators.note: something unopened has not had its front taken off, so here the first letter goes

blocks.note: bananas is slang for mad, so more bananas is madder; drop the first letter

explanation.surface: Buying a further bunch of unpeeled fruit to feed a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas is slang for crazy, so 'more bananas' is MADDER, which loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, also called the viper.

clue.text: Group of animals caught heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is cut out

blocks.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it; drop the central letter

explanation.surface: Cruel trapping of a group of beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a collective noun for a group of cattle, deer or similar animals.

clue.text: Forged tin, I note, with new design

indicators.note: forged metal is hammered into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped too

blocks.note: eight letters to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A metalworker announcing a fresh pattern beaten out of tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Design looks like the metalwork pattern but means aim, as in 'by design'.
explanation.definitionFit: Design in the sense of purpose or plan, as in 'by design', is an intention.

clue.text: Explorer departs with rifle

blocks.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
to rifle through things is to rake or search through them

explanation.surface: An adventurer setting off carrying a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Rifle is the verb meaning to search, not the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seafarer who circumnavigated the globe, a famous explorer.

clue.text: Flower in garden I left

indicators.note: in tells us the word lies inside the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of the first word and ends in the third

explanation.surface: A bloom someone abandoned in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is crossword code for a river, something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is something that flows, a river, and the Nile is Africa's great river.

clue.text: Famous Beetle car manufactured by Germany

indicators.note: manufactured goods are assembled from parts into something new, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: nine letters to be rearranged
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: The Volkswagen Beetle, Germany's renowned car.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated means widely known and praised, a direct synonym of famous.
